title: List, Dictionary, HashSet, Queue
hook: The generic collections in System.Collections.Generic are the job. An SQS batch is a list. A Redis-shaped cache is a dictionary. Choosing wrong is how you scan 50k keys on every request.

sections.heading: List<T> — growable buffer
sections.prose: List<T> is an array plus a count. Add is amortized O(1). Indexer is O(1). Insert at 0 is O(n). It is not thread-safe; two attempt-submit threads calling Add without a lock corrupt the backing store. Capacity can be set in the constructor when you know the SQS MaxNumberOfMessages. Prefer List<T> over ArrayList — ArrayList boxes value types and stores object (module 09). For a bounded in-memory buffer of CSV rows you already decided to materialize, List is correct. For a live file stream, yield instead.

snippets.label: SQS batch versus Redis map
snippets.explanation: List holds the batch. Dictionary is the cache-shaped lookup. HashSet answers membership. Queue is FIFO for retries. Four types, four questions.

sections.heading: Dictionary, HashSet, Queue, Stack
sections.prose: Dictionary<TKey, TValue> requires a hash and equality on TKey. string keys should pick a comparer: StringComparer.Ordinal for Redis-style ids, OrdinalIgnoreCase for HTTP headers. Duplicate keys throw on Add; the indexer overwrites. TryGetValue is the NRT-friendly lookup. ConcurrentDictionary is for shared mutable maps under high-concurrency — still not a distributed Redis. HashSet<T> is a dictionary without values. Queue<T> Enqueue/Dequeue is FIFO; Stack<T> is LIFO. LinkedList<T> is almost never the interview answer unless you needed O(1) unlink and already measured. ImmutableDictionary lives in System.Collections.Immutable when you publish a snapshot to many readers.

sections.heading: Thread safety and what these are not
sections.prose: None of List, Dictionary, HashSet, or Queue are safe for unsynchronized writers. A 199-to-999 concurrent attempt-submit path that shares a static Dictionary will lose entries. Use ConcurrentDictionary, a lock, or do not share. They are also not a distributed cache (Redis) and not a durable queue (SQS). Channel<T> is the in-process async pipe — named in the last topic, taught in module 15.

interviewTakeaways: Match the type to the question: append, lookup, membership, FIFO.
Generic collections avoid boxing and ArrayList’s object store.
In-process Dictionary is not Redis; in-process Queue is not SQS.
commonPitfalls: Using List.Contains in a hot loop instead of HashSet.
Forgetting a StringComparer and treating JWT issuer URLs as ordinal when they were mixed case.
Sharing a List across SQS handler tasks without synchronization.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS Array ≈ List<T>, Map ≈ Dictionary, Set ≈ HashSet. JS objects-as-maps coerce keys to strings; Dictionary does not.
Record is an object type. Dictionary<TKey,TValue> is a real hash table with struct keys allowed.
